statuses.in_bot_contradicted: in the bot, contradicted by our data
statuses.fix_engineering: a correctness fix, waiting for a reviewed change
statuses.queued: next in line for a test

tracks.E: a correctness or universe fix, by a reviewed change
tracks.F: a loss-avoiding filter, veto or exit
tracks.P: an entry that could make money: the strict exam first
tracks.R: risk and sizing: human-reviewed code only, never learnable

rules.name: Skip Mayhem coins
rules.evidence: No Mayhem check in the bot; 410 of 1,783 graduates (23%) were Mayhem coins no test covered
rules.rule: Skip Mayhem coins: CreateEvent or bonding-curve flag, supply > 1e9, or real SOL at completion < 80. Supply ≤ 1e9 does not prove non-Mayhem
rules.where: cocoon._check_mint_account gets supply from solana_rpc.mint_info and never reads it; sources/pumpfun.py returns mayhem_state
rules.refs: Lab census and lab2 universes; F3: 410 of 1,783 graduates (23%); F4 supply signature (25/25, 50/50)

rules.name: Hard fails on token authorities, extensions and pool lock
rules.evidence: Genuine graduates pass them every time (1,542 of 1,548; 100 of 100 by RPC): they carry no information
rules.rule: Provenance invariant: a coin of pump.fun origin must be Token-2022 with exactly {metadataPointer, tokenMetadata} and null mint, freeze and update authority, or it fails. Keep the blacklist for other launchpads. "Is Token-2022" carries no information
rules.where: cocoon._check_mint_account, DANGEROUS_EXTENSIONS, _apply_rug_report; the crawler accepts every Jupiter launchpad
rules.refs: F1: 1,542 of 1,548 graduates are Token-2022; F2: 100/100 by live RPC

rules.name: Measure and exit on the coin's main pool
rules.evidence: 13 of 1,783 graduates had a second pool; a second venue once cut the round trip to 0.40%
rules.rule: Measure liquidity, price and crash risk on the canonical pool only. Route exits through it unless another route is strictly better at the exact size
rules.refs: PLAN C1 engineering track (not started)

rules.name: Class each graduate: factory, operator, completed, organic
rules.evidence: Lab hypothesis G1 is registered; 450 census coins: 183 factory, 34 operator, 19 completed, 193 organic
rules.rule: G1 class at g + 140 s. OPERATOR (≥ 500 SOL of pool buys and ≤ 30 buyers in 2 min) goes to M1 only. FACTORY: instant (≤ 5 s) with top-5 share ≥ 0.85, or a ticker reused ≥ 3 times in 48 h. COMPLETED: completer or top-3 share ≥ 0.6, or < 15 buyers. "Fast fill = strong" holds only for many-wallet fills
rules.refs: lab2 G1 PREREG with 3 variants (G-time, G-chain, G-chain+) and the G1.dip and G1.R0 hosts. Debug, counts only, 450 census coins: FACTORY 183, OPERATOR 34, COMPLETED 19, ORGANIC 193, UNRESOLVED 21. RA-03's ticker variant and PE-11's "fast organic" cell are not in G1; adding them is a counted amendment

rules.name: Wait until a repeat completer has sold out
rules.evidence: Needs wallet trade data that is not downloaded yet; 24.8% of slower graduates had a completer
rules.rule: On a repeat-completer coin (completer bought ≥ 60% of the last 30 SOL, or has ≥ 3 earlier completions in a past-only registry), enter only after its position is ≤ 10% of its peak
rules.refs: lab2 S1 entry: a COMPLETED coin needs completer_pos_frac ≤ 0.10. There is no repeat-completer registry

rules.name: Serial-launcher check by creator address
rules.evidence: Only 7 of 1,145 creators launched twice; the launch counter counts platforms, not people
rules.rule: Judge a creator by its funder cluster's earlier launches (all CreateEvents, 1-2 hops, exchanges excluded), not by its address
rules.refs: lab2 G1 serial (by address, 24 h) in G-chain+

rules.name: Holder concentration caps as a rug shield
rules.evidence: Airdrops spread 0.036% over 2,200 wallets and farm rugs came from 9-13% holders (9 rugs)
rules.rule: Top-10 and single-holder caps stay hard fails only if they beat "no cap" out of sample; otherwise they become logged features
rules.refs: none

rules.name: Grade every rug-filter and radar veto
rules.evidence: Rejections are taped with rule ids, but no veto has been graded against its shadow outcome
rules.rule: Log every Cocoon and Radar veto with a shadow outcome. Grade it weekly: precision against the base loss rate, missed winners, and paired improvement with an e-process. Demote it after ≥ 200 vetoes if it shows no value; raise a drift alarm
rules.refs: The LEARNING shadow book grades strategies, not vetoes

rules.name: Jev weighs socials and paid promotion
rules.evidence: Jev's prompt asks it to; untested, and they count only if a test shows +5 points over chance
rules.rule: Socials, "DEX paid", boosts and profiles are not entry evidence unless a test shows ≥ +5 pp. Test a recent boost as a veto
rules.refs: PLAN P1 (DexScreener orders, an 18-min pull, not run). G1 NEWS and G-full are not tested (no IPFS metadata)

rules.name: Veto coins held by wallets with a rug habit
rules.evidence: Needs wallet position data: 0 coins downloaded so far
rules.rule: Veto when wallets with a learned rug habit (≥ 10 prior coins, ≥ 80% dead) hold or buy a large share
rules.refs: PLAN W1 stage 1 (does wallet skill persist?) is the go/no-go for every registry rule

rules.name: Never buy because a famous wallet bought
rules.evidence: No such trigger exists in the bot; no dated wallet lists exist to test a crowding veto
rules.rule: Never enter because a KOL or "smart" wallet bought. ≥ 3 tracked wallets buying within 5 min is a crowding veto
rules.refs: PLAN W1 stage 1. PLAN §6.6 rule 6 bans undated KOL lists and PnL leaderboards

rules.name: Measure coin age from graduation, not creation
rules.evidence: A slow graduate can be bought at graduation; random entries at 0-30 min lost 10.0% vs 6.9% at 2-6 h
rules.rule: The earliest entry is the delay after which waiting no longer improves net returns. Never enter before the BOOST bid ends (about g + 6 min). Lab rule: no entries in the first 30 min after graduation
rules.refs: RESULTS "when not to trade" (no entries in the first 30 min). PLAN §6.7 diagnostic 3 (the BOOST cliff) has not run. S1 checkpoints start at g + 6

rules.name: Enter once insiders' cheap supply is spent (S1)
rules.evidence: Lab hypothesis S1 is written but waits for wallet trade data; it ran on synthetic data only
rules.rule: Enter only when the cheap insider inventory (creator, bundle, snipers, completer, transferees) is mostly spent and organic net flow is positive: this is S1. The launch bundle share is a logged feature, not a gate
rules.refs: lab2 S1 PREREG. Its dose-response gate is exactly the PE-03 and RA-13 test, with 8 variants. Its debug ran on synthetic B1 only. RA-13's comparison (bundle_share quintiles on the same coins) is not in S1: add it as a counted descriptive

rules.name: Refuse coins with free airdropped supply
rules.evidence: Tested inside lab hypothesis G1 as a sell burst; one factory dump came 16 min after creation
rules.rule: Zero-cost supply. Refuse while transfer-in holdings or orphan sells are material. Treat identical-balance holders (≥ 10 of the top 20, or ≥ 100 identical transfers from one authority) as one holder, and the coin as FACTORY
rules.refs: lab2 G1 airdrop_seen (≥ 1,000 sell trades within ≤ 2 consecutive minutes, ≥ 3× sells to buys) in G-chain+, the bar-level proxy. S1 entry requires orphan_share10 < 0.15. Timing: the Coinbase dump came at creation + 16 min, so for instant coins it is already over by the bot's entry

rules.name: Buy confirmation on raw volume and buy/sell counts
rules.evidence: Dust bots paint both (dust share 0.80 on instant clones vs 0.09 on slow coins); the rule is untested
rules.rule: Painted volume is not demand. If more than half of the last 10 minutes' trades are dust at more than 300 trades/min, or wash wallets dominate, refuse entries triggered by volume or momentum
rules.refs: F7: dust share 0.80 on instant clones against 0.09 on slow coins; 184 of 324 instant clones were over the threshold against 0 of 304 slow coins. The F4 "winner" learned paint (A3). Partly covered by G1 FACTORY

rules.name: Count real buyers, not raw trades
rules.evidence: Factories run a median 341 trades a minute, so raw counts mislead; waits for lab data
rules.rule: Measure demand as distinct organic net buyers paying ≥ 0.01 SOL. Raw holders, trades, volume or trending rank may nominate a coin, never confirm it
rules.refs: lab2 S1 org_buyers10 and org_net10 (B1)

rules.name: No entry right after a big creator sale
rules.evidence: Rare in the bot's window: 0 of 9 farm rugs came from the creator
rules.rule: (a) No entry within 10 min of a creator or creator-funded sell of ≥ 20% of the creator's peak. (b) "Dev fully sold" is not a buy signal unless it tests positive
rules.refs: S1 entry creator_sold10 < 0.20, and its exit on a creator sell ≥ 20% of peak

rules.name: Refuse coins bought up by brand-new wallets
rules.evidence: Needs per-wallet history queries that are not written yet
rules.rule: Refuse when wallets younger than 24 h, or wallets sharing one funder, carry a large share of recent buying or of the top holdings
rules.refs: none

rules.name: Know our speed from decision to fill
rules.evidence: Never measured; lab replays 1-5 s apart were identical, so speed is probably not the weak point
rules.rule: Know our speed. Measure decision-to-fill latency (p50 and p90) and each rule's value of speed Δ(D). Reject edges that need faster fills. Build a websocket feed only if Δ(2 s) ≥ +2 pp
rules.where: Engine receipts; learn/ lag stream; POSITION_INTERVAL_S 10, WATCH_INTERVAL_S 60
rules.refs: PLAN X1 output 2 and its decision rule. RESULTS A3 and A5: 1-5 s replays were identical on farm coins, entries 1-2 min later were no worse; "latency is not the weak point"

rules.name: Creator-watch as a rug alarm
rules.evidence: 0 of 9 rugs came from the creator (too few to grade); a dump of 2,200 small sells is invisible to it
rules.rule: Label a big sell by where its tokens came from (bundle, sniper, completer, transferee or orphan seller, early top-5 pool buyer), not by the creator address. Exit at once on a distribution wave: orphan share ≥ 25% of the last 60-120 s; ≥ 20 near-identical sellers within a few slots; or SOPR3 > 2 with insider share > 0.5. While SOPR3 < 0.8 (capitulation), do not stop out on price unless the catastrophe level is hit
rules.refs: PLAN V1, folded into the S1 exits (orphan_share10 > 0.25). D1's DIST/CAP classes (module in progress, task #20)

rules.name: A danger exit must come before the crash
rules.evidence: Every radar flag exits today; farm rugs were one swap and a factory dump was over in 26 s
rules.rule: A danger signal counts as an exit only if it leads the crash by more than our exit latency on ≥ 50% of crashes and its paired effect is positive. Otherwise demote it to an entry veto and a post-mortem label. Exit signals that are kept must run at the 10 s price cadence
rules.refs: RESULTS A3: farm rugs are one swap, which no signal can lead. AUDIT: the factory dump was over in 26 s

rules.name: Stop-loss fills at the stop price in the simulators
rules.evidence: Rug stops booked at -51% to -59% really filled at -84% to -97% (36 swap windows, 9 rugs)
rules.rule: A stop is a market order. Every simulator fills stops, trails and time exits at the first trade at or after trigger + latency (B1), or at min(open, low) of the bar after the trigger bar. Never fill at the level. Log the gap slippage of every exit
rules.where: backtest.py CostModel.stop_fill; learn/replay.py exit fill; research/lab2/common.py FillConfig
rules.refs: RESULTS A3: rug stops booked at -51% to -59% were really -84% to -97%; F4 on TEST went from -5.4% to -17.7% per trade; rug-aware finalists lost -17% to -32%. X1 output 1

rules.name: Size for the -90% gap, not the -18% stop
rules.evidence: At 20% sizing one rug costs about 19% of the money, not the 3.6% the stop implies
rules.rule: Per-trade risk = ticket × L_max, where L_max = max(0.95, p95 single-swap rug loss, crash capacity 1 − (y / (y + H))²). H is the largest non-pool holder, with clusters merged. Skip the coin if its crash capacity is ≥ 0.75; refuse thin real pool SOL
rules.refs: RESULTS A3: 9 of 9 rugs were one sell of 9-13% of supply, falling 86-93% in one swap. dist_kelly: P(r ≤ −80%) = 2.2% in the worst-fill null

rules.name: Test a wide crash stop plus a time stop
rules.evidence: 7-8 of 10 test trades of the dip strategies ended at the -18% stop
rules.rule: Test a wide catastrophe stop (-35% to -50%) plus a time stop against today's -18%. Test breakeven stops but do not adopt them (prior: rejection)
rules.refs: PLAN X1 exit grid (-15%, -25%, catastrophe -50% with 60 min) and E1; lab2 G1.R0 uses X1 exit 6. F1 lost 7-8 of its 10 TEST trades to stops

rules.name: Confirm ordinary stops on a closed candle
rules.evidence: Stops fire on a touch of the 10 s price; testing it needs trade-by-trade data
rules.rule: Confirm ordinary stops on a closed bar or two polls; fire a catastrophe stop (about -40%) on touch. Only if ≥ 30% of wick breaches recover
rules.refs: PLAN X1 output 4 (stop regret)

rules.name: Set the longest hold from the crash risk by age
rules.evidence: Instant coins were stopped out 43% of the time at 0-30 min, 8% at 30-120 min, 1.2% at 2-6 h
rules.rule: Set each class's maximum hold from the crash hazard h(age, class), so that the cumulative crash probability over the hold stays ≤ 10%. Never hold through a known clock window
rules.refs: Census: the stop-out rate for instant coins falls from 43% (0-30 min) to 8% (30-120 min) to 1.2% (2-6 h). The farm's crashes cluster at g + 15-30 min

rules.name: Exit stale trades that never moved
rules.evidence: 7,631 of 9,434 random trades ended at the time limit, median -5.1%: about the trading costs
rules.rule: Stale-trade exit: if the best gain (MFE) is below Y after T minutes, exit
rules.refs: Census: 7,631 of 9,434 random trades ended at the time stop with a median of -5.1%, about the round-trip cost. An earlier exit cannot refund costs already paid

rules.name: A fixed target instead of a trailing stop
rules.evidence: On real swaps every +40% target filled at about +26%
rules.rule: Prefer a fixed target set from the host's TRAIN distribution of best gains. Keep a trailing stop only if it beats that target out of sample. Also test measuring the peak from closes instead of wick highs
rules.refs: RESULTS A3: every take-profit filled at +26% on real swaps. X1 grid

rules.name: Sell into bursts of real buying
rules.evidence: Exploratory: nothing measured yet
rules.rule: While in profit, sell into bursts of organic buying
rules.refs: none

rules.name: Sell half at +40%
rules.evidence: In the bot but never tested against a full exit or no partial; worth about 0.5 points either way
rules.rule: Keep "sell half at +X" only if it beats both a full exit and no partial out of sample. Never leave a remainder under $5
rules.refs: none

rules.name: Exit when real buying collapses
rules.evidence: Part of lab hypothesis S1's exits; waits for lab data
rules.rule: Exit when organic buying collapses: organic buy SOL over the last 5 closed minutes < 30% of the 5 minutes before entry, and distinct buyers < 50%
rules.refs: S1 exit org_net5 ≤ -1 SOL

rules.name: Exit when the dip's low breaks
rules.evidence: The dip's low is computed at entry and never used at exit
rules.rule: Thesis stop: exit when the reason for the trade flips. For dip-rebound, that is the rebound low L taken out by a closed bar
rules.refs: The PLAN and S1 PREREG exit specs for S1, D1 and M1

rules.name: Get out when the price feed goes blind
rules.evidence: A missing price leaves only the 2-hour time limit, and the blind state coincides with rugs
rules.rule: Blind means out. If there is no price, or the price is older than 30 s, use an Ultra sell quote for the whole position as the price. Two failed quotes force an exit, retried every interval
rules.refs: Jupiter Price v3 drops tokens it flags for "market health", which is the state just after a rug

rules.name: A server-side -50% stop
rules.evidence: Live only; the share of unwatched gaps is not measured yet
rules.rule: Add a server-side -50% stop (Jupiter Trigger) only if the losses in unmanaged gaps exceed its fee plus the cancel-and-withdraw latency it adds to every exit
rules.refs: PLAN X1 output 5

rules.name: Sell in one swap; alert on a bad route
rules.evidence: Exits are one swap already; the re-quote and the alert are missing
rules.rule: At $20, sell in one swap; never slice, never wait for a bounce. A quote above 3% impact means the wrong route or pool: re-quote on the canonical pool and alert
rules.refs: impact_bound.py: 0.18% at X = 102.6 SOL, 1.03% at 17.6

rules.name: Grade exits against random exit times
rules.evidence: No placebo exits yet; random entries with our exits lost 6.4% a trade
rules.rule: Exit skill = rule minus placebo exits drawn from the rule's own holding-time distribution (same entries, fills and costs). No exit rule is adopted with skill ≤ 0. Report the bot's current exits first
rules.refs: RESULTS random-entry reference: -6.4% per trade

rules.name: Stand down when the meme market breaks
rules.evidence: Results by hour swing from -59% to +26% with no pattern that holds across days
rules.rule: Regime gate (PLAN R1). Halve or stand down when the trailing 6-h single-swap rug rate is in its top 20%. Cut everything when the meme market breaks (median 15-min return ≤ -20% with > 50% of coins down, or SOL -3% in 15 min). Trade on launch heat, not the clock
rules.refs: PLAN R1 (next wave, score 20). Hour clustering was inconclusive (3 of 8 seeds at p < 0.01); the hourly ICC is about 0

rules.name: 20% sizing with a daily limit that is not a bound
rules.evidence: In simulation the 1-in-10 worst day loses 41-43% against a nominal 20% limit
rules.rule: Budget limits on Σ open ticket × L_max: a daily budget (realized + marked + open × L_max + new × L_max ≤ 15%), a drawdown floor (exposure ≤ the cushion above (1 − D) × peak), and a total-at-risk cap instead of 3 positions
rules.refs: policy_mc: the 90th-percentile worst day is 41-43% against a nominal 20%, and 13-14% with the budget rule. The cliff can end at about 78% drawdown

rules.name: Go live after 20-30 good paper trades
rules.evidence: A strategy with no real advantage passes that test about half the time at 30 trades
rules.rule: Real stake = 0 until an anytime-valid lower bound on mean net return is above 0 (the stage-2 gate: ≥ 150 paper trades over ≥ 14 days). Then at most ¼ Kelly at that bound, and at most the risk-constrained Kelly fraction on a rug-aware distribution. No funding when the trades needed to prove the edge (n*) exceed the trades available before it decays. Never go live on "20-30 positive trades"
rules.refs: LEARNING §5.4 and §5.10; sim2 and sim3; rck.py

rules.name: Get the token-account deposit back
rules.evidence: About 1.1 points of every $20 round trip go to a deposit that is never refunded
rules.rule: Reclaim token-account rent (close the account in the sell, or batch-close empty accounts) before moving to smaller tickets. Minimum ticket s_min = 4F/μ
rules.refs: PLAN C1 ("close the token account in the sell transaction regardless"), not started

rules.name: One open trade per operator family
rules.evidence: All 12 test trades of one strategy came from the same farm
rules.rule: At most one open position per operator cluster (creator, funder, factory or airdrop family, completer, or normalized ticker family), and its stake counts once
rules.refs: RESULTS §2.6: all 12 F4 TEST trades were one farm. cocrash.py: 1.23× for factory pairs against 0.75× for organic pairs (one day, weak)

rules.name: Cap the entry price impact near 0.75%
rules.evidence: At $100k and up a $20 trade moves the price about 0.1-0.3%, so the cap rarely binds
rules.rule: Cap entry impact at about 0.75%, and at ≤ ¼ of the expected edge. Skip quotes whose impact is more than 2× the constant-product prediction from the reserves
rules.refs: ticket_costs.py; RESULTS A4 (quotes within 0.0-0.35 pp of the model)

rules.name: Step live size up slowly
rules.evidence: Only matters once something shows a real advantage
rules.rule: Live ladder: start at the minimum ticket and step up ×1.5 per 50 live trades, only while the paper-live twin gap is ≥ -1 pp, the CUSUM is quiet, and G39 allows
rules.refs: LEARNING §5.4 and §7

rules.name: Sweep gains above about $125 to the owner
rules.evidence: Today the $150 wallet cap stops the bot once it does well
rules.rule: Sweep equity above about $125 to the owner and never refill after losses. Base the wallet tripwire on equity attributed to the bot, not a fixed $150
rules.refs: sim2 part c (sweeping: median $111; compounding: $92, decaying edge)

rules.name: Judge decay on per-trade returns
rules.evidence: At 20% sizing even a real +3% strategy hits a 30% drawdown in simulation
rules.rule: Judge edge decay with the CUSUM / e-process on per-trade returns, which does not depend on sizing. Set the equity backstop from the current sizing, so that a real edge hits it with ≤ 5% probability
rules.refs: LEARNING §5.5; sim2 (at 20% sizing, a real +3% edge hits a 30% drawdown 100% of the time)

rules.name: No tilt or streak sizing
rules.evidence: After 3 losses the next trade averaged -6.7% vs -6.5% overall (one day of data)
rules.rule: No tilt, equity-curve or anti-martingale sizing unless a streak effect is shown
rules.refs: dp_results.json, reentry_results.json

rules.name: Jev's no-votes must catch more than chance
rules.evidence: Never graded: vetoed coins are not followed up
rules.rule: Jev keeps its veto only if, on coins that passed every deterministic rule, its "no" votes land on later rugs and losers more often than a random veto at the same rate, net of API cost. Its confidence must be calibrated and its verdicts repeatable (≥ 80%). It sees numeric fingerprints (class, crash capacity, dust share, orphan share, insider_rem), never just names
rules.refs: none

rules.name: Clean the trade data before any wallet rule
rules.evidence: Mostly done in research; a few exclusion lists and checks are still missing
rules.rule: Evidence hygiene before any wallet or flow rule: drop failed transactions; exclude pooled accounts; read has_create = 0 as NULL; price at (x + v) / y with v per trade; handle PostCompleteBuyEvent
rules.refs: AUDIT fixes 1-6, tested

rules.name: Trip wires on protocol constants
rules.evidence: PumpSwap events grew 8 bytes on Oct 3; only one constant is checked today
rules.rule: Protocol-constant tripwires: BOOST (17.5845 SOL, 29-30 slices), migration reserves (85 SOL / 206.9M), curve supply (793.1M), the sign of v, the Mayhem share, event lengths and a fee-page hash. On a breach, freeze promotions and re-validate every detector that depends on it
rules.refs: AUDIT §3.2 and §3.7 (PumpSwap events grew 8 bytes on 10-03); RESULTS (the farm's timing drifted)

rules.name: A post-mortem for every trade
rules.evidence: Not built yet; the parts of each result must add up to the trade
rules.rule: Post-mortem every closed trade within 24 h: paper, live, and shadow trades with a ≥ 50% drawdown. Record: the class (C3-C14, or ordinary bleed), with the earliest second it was knowable against our decision second; best and worst points (MFE/MAE), exit efficiency, gap slippage and stop regret; and an additive P&L split (selection, timing, exit, execution, residual) assigned to the member that controls each part. Thresholds fixed in advance open re-tests; they never change parameters automatically
rules.refs: RESULTS: 9 labelled rug exits and 36 F4 swap windows

rules.name: Call a loss a mistake only against matched trades
rules.evidence: Re-entry after a stop looked 4.6 points worse raw but 0.4 [-1.8, +1.1] matched: it was coin age
rules.rule: Compare a suspected mistake only with trades in the same situation (speed class, age band, G1 class, market-cap tier, regime). A mistake becomes a candidate rule only with ≥ 10 instances, ≥ 5 operators, ≥ 3 days, and a matched gap whose CI excludes 0. Adoption needs PLAN §3.5's veto bar. A single loss never patches the bot, except for pipeline bugs (G52)
rules.refs: reentry_results.json: re-entry after a stop looked -4.6 pp worse raw and -0.4 pp [-1.8, +1.1] matched. The apparent "mistake" was coin age

rules.name: Hunt for bugs after an unusually bad loss
rules.evidence: Every material error the lab audits found so far was a pipeline error
rules.rule: An unusually bad loss (below the 1% quantile of the variant's replay distribution) starts with a bug hunt: decision fidelity, data freshness, price, fills against quotes, costs, lookahead. A pipeline fault is the only kind of mistake fixed after a single instance
rules.refs: So far, every material error the lab audits found was a pipeline error: the half fill, the SOL/USD lookahead, a constant v, the truncated AGENT window, NULL read as 0

rules.name: Count independent situations, not raw reps
rules.evidence: 16 random entries in one coin are worth about 5.4 independent ones
rules.rule: Count experience as the effective number of independent, outcome-known episodes per situation cell: n_eff = n / (1 + (m̄ − 1) × ICC), by coin, operator and day. Do not call a member "experienced" in a cell below the n needed to detect a 5 pp effect
rules.refs: dp_results: coin ICC 0.13, so 16 random entries per coin are worth about 5.4 independent ones. F4's 12 TEST trades amount to about 1 operator

rules.name: Practise only where the pattern holds day to day
rules.evidence: The farm's crash share moved from 22-24% to 33% between splits
rules.rule: Practise only on learnable cells: the sign holds across days and operators (I² < 50%, ≥ 75% of days with the same sign) and feedback is fast. Cells driven by one operator get vetoes only
rules.refs: RESULTS: the farm's 15-30-min crash share moved from 22-24% to 33% between splits

rules.name: Grade decisions by expected value, never by one result
rules.evidence: A rule with no advantage still comes out ahead on 79% of single trades
rules.rule: Grade decisions by the out-of-sample expected value of their (rule, cell), never by win rate or by one outcome
rules.refs: dp_results: a zero-edge rule wins 79% of single trades; a +5% rule loses 14%; cells explain 4.7% of single-trade variance

rules.name: Seal a numeric plan before each entry
rules.evidence: A simple per-situation forecast of stop-outs scored 0.19 over no forecast, but was miscalibrated
rules.rule: Seal a numeric plan in each entry receipt, and each shadow skip or veto, before the fill: rule hash, cell, thesis features, invalidation, horizon, size, assumed rug-aware worst loss, P(take-profit before stop), P(single-swap drop ≥ 50%), and expected net return with its CI
rules.refs: brier_results: a trivial cell forecast of stop-outs reached Brier skill 0.19 [0.15, 0.23] from census TRAIN to VAL, but was miscalibrated (forecast 0.16, observed 0.29 in one bin)

rules.name: Sealed exams for every skill claim
rules.evidence: One strategy made +14% in practice, -5.4% on its exam and -17.7% on real swaps
rules.rule: Practise on a simulator with sealed exams: search on train, VAL from a shortlist written in advance, one TEST pass, every configuration logged and deflated (DSR, CSCV/PBO). Every claim that a member is skilled (turning Jev on, trusting a Cocoon forecast, a new exit) spends α like a strategy does
rules.refs: RESULTS: F4 made +14% in practice, -5.4% on the exam and -17.7% on real swaps

rules.name: One report card per member against a random stand-in
rules.evidence: Being built: a card says no measurable skill until its band clears chance
rules.rule: One report card per member against a no-skill baseline, with an anytime-valid CI. Crawler: G60. Cocoon: pass-minus-reject shadow return against a random veto at the same rate (and per rule via G08). Strategy: against a matched random entry. Radar: G21. Jev: G47. Broker: G59. Risk: limit breaches, gap ratio, rug-rate calibration, realistic drawdowns. Exits: G36. Coach: the placebo loses, a planted edge is found, false promotions stay in bound. A card says "skilled" only when its lower bound beats the baseline
rules.refs: LEARNING §9

rules.name: Score each fill by its shortfall
rules.evidence: Entry drift averaged +0.2% at 2 s; rug stop losses are a rug problem, not an execution one
rules.rule: Score each fill by its implementation shortfall against the mid at decision time: delay, impact plus fees, and the opportunity cost of missed signals. Compare paper with its replay twin, and later live with paper
rules.refs: RESULTS A1 and A3: entry drift averaged +0.2% at 2 s (at most 0.9%). Rug stops are structural, a Risk and Cocoon problem, not an execution one

rules.name: Measure which new coins the crawler sees
rules.evidence: The bot watches at most 15 of about 1,200 graduates a day; coverage is not measured
rules.rule: Coverage: recall of tradeable graduates within 5, 15 and 60 min against CryptoHouse CompleteEvents, the median lag, and the reason for each miss. Check that the shadow returns of missed coins match those of seen ones
rules.refs: none

rules.name: State rug odds as probabilities
rules.evidence: Pass or fail only today
rules.rule: State probabilities. Cocoon: P(single-swap drop ≥ 50% or airdrop dump during the hold). Radar: P(drop ≥ 30% in 5 min). Score them by Brier and log loss, and recalibrate weekly on past weeks only. Hard fails stay fail-closed
rules.refs: The G56 demo

rules.name: Spend practice on the weakest situations
rules.evidence: Random entries 0-30 min after an instant graduation lost 15.7% (a situation the bot never trades)
rules.rule: Give part of the 4 weekly registrations to the weakest learnable cell (ranked by G50's attribution), judged forward only. Keep this only if it beats a uniform allocation
rules.refs: Census: instant coins 0-30 min after graduation lost -15.7% per random entry, stopped out 43% of the time (a cell the bot never trades)

rules.name: The default dip-rebound strategy
rules.evidence: It lost on every split and every stress test; its one exam trade lost 22.1%
rules.rule: The default dip-rebound itself. It made 1 TEST trade (-22.1%), and the F1 dip strategies lost on every split and every stress test.
rules.where: strategy.entry_signal (dip-rebound); DIP_PCT and the other strategy Settings
rules.refs: RESULTS F1 (the dip strategies); the lab1 judge's one TEST trade
